name: Dwell
subtitle: Student living, connected.
scope: Research, resident app, website & design system
content: The Big Idea: To transform the student living experience by replacing fragmented processes with a centralized, intuitive digital ecosystem. The core mission was to bridge the gap between physical property management and student convenience, creating a “home in your pocket.”

My Role (Lead UX/UI Designer): I led the end-to-end design strategy, transforming complex property management workflows into a frictionless mobile experience. My focus was on reducing cognitive load for residents while increasing operational efficiency for property staff.
User-Centric Architecture: Conducted user research to identify pain points in daily student life, directly informing the app’s navigation and feature prioritization.
Systems Thinking: Developed a cohesive design system that ensures consistency across mobile and web touchpoints, allowing for rapid scaling and future feature integration.

Functional Design: Designed intuitive interfaces for high-frequency tasks—such as facility booking, maintenance requests, and digital access—drastically reducing the time students spend managing their day-to-day residence needs.

I synthesized user research from multiple student respondents to identify key behavioral archetypes. I mapped their demographics, academic goals, and tech literacy levels to create five distinct personas.

These personas served as our “North Star” throughout the design process, ensuring that features like the room booking flow and support options were tailored to the specific anxieties and needs of international vs. local students.

Based on the user journeys defined by the personas, I structured the site’s information architecture to prioritize “findability.” I mapped the hierarchy from the global country selector down to granular property and room-specific pages.
I created a logical, scalable navigation structure that reduces user friction, allowing students to navigate from “discovery” to “booking” with the minimum number of clicks.

Before diving into high-fidelity visuals, I established the skeleton of the platform. I focused on accessibility and clear information hierarchy, ensuring that critical data points—like pricing, room types, and availability—remained consistent across all property levels. This phase was crucial for validating the user flow with stakeholders before the final design implementation.

To support Dwell’s global expansion, I developed a modern, scalable design system. This involved defining a vibrant yet professional color palette, a rigorous typographic scale, and a library of reusable UI components. This “single source of truth” ensures that future features can be developed rapidly while maintaining a consistent and premium brand experience.

The mobile app was designed as the central companion for every Dwell resident. I focused on making high-stress tasks—like reporting maintenance issues or managing rent payments—as frictionless as possible. The goal was to provide a sense of security and community right in the student's pocket, bridging the gap between their physical home and their digital life.
I integrated a secure parcel locker system with automated notifications to solve the pain point of missed deliveries.

Maintenance requests are streamlined through a dedicated portal. By allowing residents to attach photos and track ticket status, I improved transparency and reduced anxiety regarding the resolution of property issues.
To foster a sense of belonging, I created a social hub for property announcements and event RSVPs. This transforms the residence from a simple building into a connected student community.

This feature provides a transparent hub for students to manage their residency. Residents can view real-time account statements, check payment history, and make secure rent payments directly through the app, simplifying financial management.

name: EPIISOD
subtitle: A new standard of student living.
content: To redefine student accommodation by launching EPIISOD—a premium, tech-forward brand. The mission was to move beyond "lodgings" and create an integrated lifestyle experience where smart technology, wellness, and community are managed through a single, sophisticated digital touchpoint.

I led the end-to-end design strategy for the EPIISOD brand launch. My focus was on creating a high-end digital identity that mirrors the luxury of the physical properties, ensuring that complex IoT features (like mobile room access and smart climate control) feel intuitive for every resident.

Premium User Architecture: I architected a user journey that emphasizes the “EPIISOD Experience," prioritizing high-value perks like wellness bookings and smart-room controls to differentiate the brand from standard housing.

Experience-Led Design: Designed interfaces for the flagship Sydney property that allow students to manage everything from their rooftop infinity pool access to weekday breakfast perks with zero friction.

The EPIISOD app is the heart of the resident’s stay. I focused on integrating tech-driven features like smart keyless entry and IoT room controls with everyday essentials like parcel notifications and account management. The goal was to provide residents with total control and peace of mind, making the “EPIISOD Experience” a reality.

To match EPIISOD’s high-end physical architecture, I developed a sophisticated design system. This included a refined color palette and a modern typographic scale that reflects “Elevation” and "Innovation," ensuring a premium feel across every digital interaction.

name: EPIISOD Redesign
subtitle: Quiet luxury, made for students.
scope: Website redesign, immersive property experience & design system
content: The Big Idea: To give EPIISOD a website as considered as its buildings. The brand launched in July 2025 as Centurion’s elevated, design-led student living label, and its website needed to say that before a single room was seen. The redesign turns the site into the first room a student walks into: warm, calm and quietly confident.

My Role (Lead UX/UI Designer): I led the redesign end to end, from information architecture and visual language to interaction design, and shaped a working, deployed prototype so the team could feel every scroll, transition and booking step rather than imagine it.

The Work: A new home page, Find a Room search, property and room pages, an immersive experience page for Macquarie Park, a resident-app showcase, an AI assistant, and the Student Luxe design system that holds it all together.
A launch site that needed to grow up

The first EPIISOD site was built to launch quickly. It listed rooms and promotions, but it could not yet carry the feeling of the buildings: the warm timber, the soft light and the quiet confidence of the spaces.
The brief I set: One story told consistently across every page, a path from curiosity to enquiry in as few steps as possible, and a visual language that feels premium without feeling distant.

Who it is for: International students choosing from overseas, local students comparing places near campus, and parents who want reassurance. Each audience gets its own way in through dedicated blogs, FAQs, language choice and a guided assistant.

How we did it: I built the system around three ideas. Warm paper instead of white, deep ink instead of black, and a single muted bronze for everything that deserves attention. Libre Baskerville carries the voice, with italics reserved for the one word that matters in each headline. DM Sans keeps forms, prices and labels calm and legible.

Built to flex: Colour, type, corners and spacing live in design tokens. Curved or sharp corners, a light or dark theme and three languages can be switched from one settings panel without touching a single component, which made it easy to try the brand in different moods with stakeholders.

Accessible by default: Bronze text uses a deeper shade so small labels pass WCAG AA contrast on every cream surface, focus states are always visible, and parallax and scroll effects switch off for people who prefer reduced motion.

How we did it: The home page replaces a stack of banners with one paced sequence. A hero that goes straight to Find a Room, a locations carousel, a brand film that grows from a small thumbnail into a full frame, a collage of student life and a pinned wellness story.

Small moments of delight: A metal EPIISOD coin spins in real time and splits the closing lines like liquid as you scroll past. The footer wordmark assembles from the emblem, with its arcs swinging into place. Each one is small, but together they make the brand feel crafted.
What we achieved: A home page that puts the product first, with search, locations and the brand film all one scroll away, while keeping a calm enough pace to feel premium.
From a vague idea to a shortlist

How we did it: Students rarely start with a room type. They start with a university, a city and a weekly budget. Find a Room is built around that, with city, institution, room type, price range and lease term, and a results line that always says how many rooms match and the lowest weekly price.
No dead ends: Rooms in properties that have not opened yet say “Opening Semester 2, 2027 · Register interest” instead of disappearing, so the waitlist grows while the buildings are still being built.
One search, everywhere: The same search sits on the home page and at the top of every property page, so a student can refine their options without starting again.
Everything to decide, in one place

How we did it: A property page leads with the building, using a 3D model of the façade, then moves through amenities, rooms, location, promotions and FAQs, held together by a floating sub-navigation. A room page answers the same questions in the same order every time: gallery, overview, specs, what is included, floor plan and location.

Booking that follows you: A booking card travels with the reader down the page, so the next step is never more than a glance away, while “Enter the experience” invites students who want to feel the property first.

Maps that help: A “places nearby” map lists transport, food, schools, shopping and medical services within a chosen walking distance, so international students can picture a normal week before they arrive.
Walk through the building before you visit

How we did it: A second, immersive page for the flagship property. A guided tour of four moments leads into a curved 3D carousel of amenities, a blueprint-style reveal where line drawings become photographs, and an aerial view that marks the university, shopping centre and station with their walking times.
Sketch to photograph: Architectural line drawings give way to the finished rooms as you drag, a nod to the process behind the building and a way to show students what they are really getting.
Dark and light: The page ships in both a light and a dark look, switched with a small sun and moon button, and remembers the choice.

How we did it: The experience page closes the loop with the EPIISOD Living app. Amenities, parcels, discovery, maintenance, payments and Resi-Life events are each one tap away on a phone mock-up that visitors can explore.

A smart room you can try: Drag the phone to move it, tap a light and watch the room respond, or switch the air-conditioning from the app. On a phone, visitors can enable tilt to move through the 3D scenes.

EPIISOD Assistant: A chat assistant answers questions about rooms, prices, offers and what is included, then hands over to booking or to the team. It draws only on EPIISOD’s own content, so answers stay accurate and on brand.

Language and settings: The whole site can switch between English, Chinese and Hindi, remembered on the device. A prototype settings panel lets stakeholders change corner style, theme and whether other properties show as coming soon or ready.

Designed for phones: Navigation becomes a full-screen menu with language choices, search fields stack into one column, room cards become a vertical feed, and the experience page adds touch gestures such as swipe, drag and tilt.

Craft and performance: Every page loads only the code it needs, the 3D coin loads only when it is about to appear, and images are sized for how they are shown. Scroll effects use GSAP and Lenis, with motion reduced for those who ask for it.
How it was built: A working React, TypeScript and Vite prototype deployed on Vercel, so stakeholders could test the real thing in a browser as early as possible instead of reviewing static screens.
What I learned: Premium is mostly restraint. Every effect earns its place by helping a student understand the building, the price or the next step.

name: Ohmyhome
subtitle: Making property feel simple.
content: The Big Idea: Ohmyhome set out to shake up the property market across Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines. The goal was simple: make buying, selling, or renting a home truly easy, transparent, and affordable for everyone. A Fresh Start: What’s unique here is that Ohmyhome was built from the ground up – there were no existing designs when I joined. The entire digital experience, for both the app and website, grew directly from my design work. It was an exciting challenge to lay the digital foundation for a brand-new business. My Role: Lead UX & Product Designer (Founding Product Designer) . I was deeply involved in shaping the entire user experience and product direction from day one. This meant getting hands-on with research, defining the information architecture, designing core user flows, contributing to the product roadmap, and collaborating closely with the founding team and engineers.

Launching Ohmyhome meant designing the entire digital engine for a new business. We faced the challenge of creating an intuitive platform from scratch that could: • Bring transparency to property dealings (pricing, agents). • Offer a reliable property valuation tool. • Seamlessly integrate renovation and insurance services. • Establish clear, trustworthy communication channels. • Most importantly, validate the entire business concept through design.
As the Lead UX & Product Designer , I defined and drove a user-centered design process from conception to launch.
• Deep Dive Research: We started with foundational user research (interviews, surveys, competitor analysis) to understand core needs and validate assumptions for this new product.
Strategic Design: Based on insights, I crafted the information architecture and core user flows (app & web), creating wireframes and prototypes that formed the very blueprint of Ohmyhome.
User Validation: Rigorous usability testing was crucial. We ran early tests with prototypes, iterating constantly to refine the experience and ensure it met user needs.
The Idea: We flipped the traditional property search. “Shoutout” let buyers post what they were looking for , empowering sellers to actively find matching buyers, rather than just waiting.

My Role: I designed the user flow and interface that enabled buyers to create their “Shoutout” and, crucially, allowed sellers to browse and respond to these requests, opening up a new pathway for connections.
The Win: This feature was a game-changer, driving an amazing 75% increase in app usage for users engaging with the Shoutout feature, significantly enhancing the marketplace’s dynamism.

The Idea: Our research showed a huge pain point: users on other platforms rarely got replies from sellers and landlord. We built a dedicated in-app chat to fix this, enabling direct communication, offer exchange, and appointment setting. And we incentivised posters that replies and are active by promoting their listings more.

My Role: I designed the comprehensive chat experience, including features that prioritised active posters . This not only ensured users connected with responsive parties but also provided us with valuable insights into transaction patterns.

The Win: This created a reliable and transparent communication channel, reducing user frustration from unanswered messages by 60% and leading to a 35% increase in daily active users engaging in property-related conversations.
The Idea: We wanted to give sellers and landlords full control and smart insights for their property listings. So, we created a dedicated dashboard just for them.

My Role: I designed the dashboard's layout and functionality, integrating tools like our free valuation service directly into their management experience. This allowed owners to leverage data for optimal pricing strategies.

The Win: Owners could effortlessly manage listings and find the best price using real data, leading to a 25% increase in listings managed through the dashboard and contributing to a 10% growth in daily active usage among sellers/landlords.

name: Cora
subtitle: One ecosystem. Every perspective.
content: CORA is an innovative cloud-based platform for property managers and owners, designed to streamline operations, enhance tenant communication, and enable data-driven decisions for enhanced efficiency and service.
- Simplified Resident Onboarding: Effortless tenant registration and lease management, with seamless rent collection and payment tracking.
- Streamlined Maintenance Tracking: Efficiently track maintenance requests, repair statuses, and generate insightful reports on maintenance costs.
- Effortless Fee Collection: Easy fee collection through online payments and seamless processing.
- Comprehensive Property Reporting: Valuable insights on rent collection, tenant turnover, and other key performance indicators for property managers.
- Effective Communication Tools: Seamless interactions between tenants and property managers for positive tenant relationships.
Powerful all in one web app for property management
The Idea: A comprehensive web-based dashboard for property managers and owners to oversee all operations, from lease management to financial reporting.

My Contribution: I focused on designing the intuitive layout and complex data visualization for lease management, rent collection tracking, and comprehensive property reporting, giving managers clear insights.

The Win: This dashboard became managers' central command, leading to 1-2 Hour faster data access for reports ( from manual Reporting and CSV reporting ) and [20]% over all reduction in time spent on lease management , significantly boosting operational efficiency. And greatly minimized human errors.
The Idea: A mobile app designed to simplify the living experience for tenants, from onboarding to rent payments and maintenance requests.

My Contribution: I designed the seamless user flows for resident onboarding, effortless rent collection (online payments), streamlined maintenance request submission, and easy communication with managers.

The Win: This intuitive app led to a at least a [60]% smoother resident experience ( based on resident survey ) , a [15]% increase in on-time rent payments , ( for non auto debit accounts ) and significantly enhanced tenant satisfaction ( based on resident reviews ) through simplified interactions.
The Idea: A dedicated mobile app for on-site staff (e.g., maintenance teams) to efficiently track and manage tasks, communicate, and update statuses from anywhere.

My Contribution: I focused on designing the streamlined maintenance tracking flows, real-time status updates, and effective communication tools specifically for the staff app, optimizing their daily tasks.
The Win: Empowered staff to be more efficient, resulting in a [83]% faster response time to maintenance requests and [70%]% improved task completion rates , directly enhancing service quality.

Holistic Impact: The CORA platform successfully launched, creating a truly unified and efficient experience for property managers, owners, residents, and staff. My design work directly contributed to streamlining operations and fostering better relationships across the property ecosystem.

My Key Learning: This project was incredibly rewarding, reinforcing the power of designing for multiple, interconnected user types within a single ecosystem. Understanding each user’s unique workflow and communication needs was crucial to delivering a truly impactful, streamlined platform .

name: myElite.pro
subtitle: Tools for the people behind the property.
role: Lead UX Designer · UX Researcher · Product Designer
content: As a UX designer, I had the opportunity to work on myELITE.pro, a property platform that lets you earn incentives by referring clients. It offers access to over 40,000 units from nearly 200 developers, making it easy to find the perfect property for your clients. The platform also provides support from a team of real estate professionals to help you achieve your earning goals.
1. Easy Referral System: We designed a simple step-by-step referral process, allowing you to invite clients effortlessly and track your earnings.
2. Diverse Property Selection: With thousands of properties available, we ensured a user-friendly interface with smart search options and detailed property profiles for seamless exploration.
3. Expert Support: Access to a team of real estate professionals who can assist and guide you on your journey to earning incentives.
4. Stay Informed: Keep up with the latest real estate trends through informative articles and market insights.
5. Build Your Network: Connect with other real estate professionals through discussion forums, meetups, and virtual events.

The user interface is clean and modern, reflecting the platform’s professionalism and trustworthiness. The design is optimized for both the app and website, ensuring a consistent experience across different devices.
The Idea: With over 40,000 units Across the country , users needed a clear, efficient way to find the perfect property for their clients. and a easy way to view the properties details.

My Role: I designed the user-friendly interface for the extensive property database, including smart search options, robust filtering capabilities, and detailed property profiles for seamless exploration. Plus these project details pages are shareable via Social media.
Flexible filter function to help sellers find the best property for their clients
The Idea: With over 40,000 units Across the country , users needed a clear, efficient way to find the perfect property for their clients. and a easy way to view the properties details.

My Role: I designed the user-friendly interface for the extensive property database, including smart search options, robust filtering capabilities, and detailed property profiles for seamless exploration. Plus these project details pages are shareable via Social media.
Your Command Center Robust Property Search

The Idea: Agents needed a clear, efficient way to manage all their clients and track their team's progress with each one. This helps them stay on top of client funnel stages and assist teammates effectively.

My Role: I designed the comprehensive client management module, including client profiles, funnel stage tracking, and team collaboration views. My goal was to provide a real-time overview for individual agents and their teams.

Impactful Launch: MyELITE.pro successfully launched, providing a powerful platform that genuinely empowers users to achieve their earning goals through referrals. The clean, modern UI reflects its professionalism and trustworthiness across both app and website.
Key Metrics of Success Overall: Enhanced property discovery, leading to a 40 % increase in users utilizing advanced search filters and a 32% higher engagement rate with detailed property profiles .

My Key Learning: This project highlighted the importance of designing not just for a transaction, but for an entire ecosystem of support, information, and community. Simplifying a complex incentive model through intuitive design was key to user adoption and success.
